recognize_zh: 骨髓切片中多顆組織球細胞質內塞滿許多 2–4 µm 的小圓形酵母，每顆周圍有透明暈圈（假莢膜）並可見偏位的月牙形小核，部分游離於細胞外；組織球內大量均一小酵母，符合莢膜組織漿菌（Histoplasma capsulatum）感染。
features: Histiocytes distended by numerous small, uniform, round to oval yeast forms (about 2-4 um)
Each yeast with a clear halo (pseudocapsule) around a small, dot-like or crescentic basophilic nucleus
Clusters of yeasts within cytoplasmic vacuoles and occasional extracellular organisms
Mixed background of hematopoietic cells, plasma cells and interstitial histiocytes
Large fat spaces at the edges of the field; H&E stain
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy shows an interstitial histiocytic infiltrate among residual hematopoietic cells and fat. Many histiocytes contain clusters of small, uniform, round to oval yeast forms measuring approximately 2-4 um, each with a clear halo and a small crescentic nucleus, and occasional organisms appear extracellular. Well-formed granulomas and necrosis are not evident in this field. The findings are consistent with disseminated histoplasmosis, and confirmation with GMS/PAS stains, culture or urine antigen is recommended.

ddx.vs: Leishmania amastigotes have both a nucleus and a rod-shaped kinetoplast, lack a clear halo, and are GMS/PAS-negative, whereas Histoplasma is GMS-positive with narrow-based budding.
Talaromyces yeasts divide by fission with a central transverse septum and include elongated sausage forms, unlike budding Histoplasma.
Cryptococcus is larger and more variable (4-10 um) with a thick mucicarmine-positive capsule.
Toxoplasma tachyzoites are crescentic without halos and Pneumocystis cysts are extracellular cup-shaped forms, neither filling histiocytes with haloed yeasts.
